title: They say it is Allah's. Then why not remember?
subtitle: Knowing the answer but not living it
then: Ibn Kathir says they {reward}admitted the earth belongs to Allah alone{/reward}. So the Prophet ﷺ was told to ask: {idea}will you not then remember that none should be worshipped except the Creator and Provider?{/idea}
now: You would answer "Allah" in a quiz without thinking. Then you spend the day as if the rent, the boss, and your own effort run everything. {idea}The answer is in your head; the verse wants it in your day.{/idea}
old: I already know Allah owns everything.
new: Knowing it is the start; remembering it all day is the point.
try: Set one reminder on your phone today that says: it all belongs to Allah.

title: Who is Lord of the seven heavens and the Great Throne?
subtitle: The question rises higher
then: The question moves from the earth to the sky. Ibn Kathir describes {idea}the higher realm with its planets, lights and angels{/idea}, and the Throne as {reward}the highest of all created things, combining height, vastness and splendor{/reward}. Ibn Masud said the Throne's light is from the light of His Face.
now: The bill, the exam, the argument with your sister: they fill the whole screen of your mind. {idea}Zoom out. The One you pray to is Lord of the Great Throne.{/idea}
old: My problems are bigger than anything else.
new: My Lord is the Lord of the Great Throne, and my problem is small to Him.
try: Before you worry about something today, say: Allah is Lord of the Great Throne. Then ask Him.

title: Again they say Allah. Then will you not be mindful?
subtitle: From remembering to fearing
then: The first reply was {idea}will you not remember?{/idea} Now the response grows: {idea}will you not have taqwa?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says: since you admit He is Lord of the heavens and the Throne, {trap}will you not fear His punishment for worshipping others with Him?{/trap}
now: You say "Allah is great" forty times a day in prayer. Then in the office kitchen you laugh along with a joke you know is wrong. {idea}Admitting His greatness should change how you act when He is the only one watching.{/idea}
old: Saying Allah is great is enough.
new: If I truly admit His greatness, I should be mindful of Him.
try: Pick one moment today when you would normally slip, and pause to remember He sees.

title: He protects, and no one can protect against Him.
subtitle: The control of everything is in His hand
then: Ibn Kathir explains that among the Arabs, if a leader gave someone protection, {idea}no one could go against it{/idea}, yet someone could still protect against that leader. {reward}Allah is the greatest Master; none can overturn His ruling.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ would swear: by the One who turns the hearts.
now: You are scared of a manager who could end your contract, or a person who has power over your family. {idea}They are held by Someone too.{/idea} His protection is the only one nobody can override.
old: I need the right people on my side to be safe.
new: Only Allah's protection cannot be overruled, so I seek it first.
try: When you feel threatened today, say: Hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: They say Allah a third time. So how are you fooled?
subtitle: The final question of the three
then: Three questions, three times they answer: Allah. The last reply is sharpest: {trap}how then are you deceived?{/trap} Ibn Kathir: {trap}how can your minds accept worshipping others when you recognize and acknowledge this?{/trap}
now: You know scrolling at midnight wrecks your morning. You know the sale is a trap. You know the grudge hurts you most. {trap}Knowing is not the same as being free.{/trap} Something keeps fooling you.
old: If I know the truth, I am not being fooled.
new: I can know the truth and still be fooled, so I must act on what I know.
try: Name one thing you know is wrong for you but still do. Take one step away from it today.

title: We brought them the truth, and they are lying.
subtitle: Partners with no evidence

row.title: the truth
sub: no god but Allah, with proof

then: Ibn Kathir says the truth is {idea}the declaration that there is no god but Allah, with clear and sound proof{/idea}. They are liars in worshipping others {trap}with no evidence, only following confused forefathers{/trap}: we found our fathers on a way and we follow it.
now: "That's how my family has always done it." A habit at weddings, a belief about luck, a way of treating people. {idea}Ask: is there proof for this, or only tradition?{/idea}
old: If my family always did it, it must be right.
new: I check what I follow against the truth, not only against custom.
try: Pick one family habit and ask yourself honestly whether it has a real basis.

title: If there were other gods, the universe would fall to fighting.
subtitle: The order of the world points to One
then: Ibn Kathir says if there were many gods, {trap}each would control what he created, so there would be no order{/trap}. But {idea}the universe is ordered and cohesive, upper and lower realms connected perfectly{/idea}. Allah has no son and no partner.
now: Two managers giving opposite instructions, and the whole project collapses. You have seen it at work. {idea}The sky has never had that problem.{/idea}
old: The universe just happens to be orderly.
new: The order I see everywhere points to one Lord alone.
try: Look at one ordered thing today, a leaf, your heartbeat, the clock of the sun, and say: subhanallah.

title: He knows the hidden and the seen.
subtitle: Exalted above any partner
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}He knows what is hidden from His creatures and what they see{/idea}. That is why He is {reward}sanctified, glorified and exalted above all that the wrongdoers say{/reward}.
now: The thought you never said out loud. The reason behind the favor you did. The tears in the car before you walked in smiling. {idea}All of it is known to Him.{/idea}
old: People only know what I show them.
new: Allah knows what I show and what I hide, and I can be honest with Him.
try: Tell Allah tonight about one thing you have hidden from everyone.

title: If You show me what they are promised, my Lord.
subtitle: A dua taught for times of trial
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}commands His Prophet ﷺ to call on Him with this supplication when calamity strikes{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ also taught: {reward}if You want to test people, take me to You without being put through the trial.{/reward}
now: When things fall apart around you, a company scandal, a family feud, people you warned now facing the result, {trap}it is easy to feel "I told you so."{/trap} {idea}The verse turns you to ask for your own safety instead.{/idea}
old: When wrongdoers face consequences, I should feel vindicated.
new: When trials come, my concern is my own safety with Allah.
try: When you hear of someone's downfall today, ask Allah to protect you from the same.

title: Then do not put me among the wrongdoing people.
subtitle: Even the Prophet ﷺ asked for this

row.title: everyone
sub: the Prophet ﷺ was taught it

then: Ibn Kathir explains the meaning: {idea}if You punish them while I am witnessing, then do not cause me to be one of them.{/idea} The best of creation was taught to ask {reward}not to be counted with the wrongdoers{/reward}.
now: You think of yourself as one of the good ones. Then you notice how easily you slid into the office gossip, the unfair joke, the group that excludes someone. {idea}Nobody is too good for this dua.{/idea}
old: I am not the kind of person who becomes a wrongdoer.
new: I ask Allah every day not to let me slide into wrong.
try: Add this dua to your prayer today: Rabbi fa la taj'alni fil qawmiz-zalimin.

title: We are able to show you what We promised them.
subtitle: Delay is not inability
then: Ibn Kathir says: {idea}if We willed, We could show you the punishment and test We will send upon them.{/idea} Delay was His choice, {reward}not a lack of power{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ was being comforted.
now: You have watched someone cheat and prosper, lie and get promoted. It feels like nobody is keeping score. {idea}Allah is able. He has not forgotten.{/idea} Your job is your own conduct.
old: If wrong is not punished now, maybe it never will be.
new: Allah is able, and His timing is His, so I leave it with Him.
try: Hand one injustice that eats at you over to Allah in dua, and let it go for today.

title: Push back their evil with what is better.
subtitle: Answering harm with kindness
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {idea}the best way to behave when mixing with people: treat kindly the one who treats you badly, to soften his heart{/idea}. He cites: then the one with enmity becomes {reward}like a close friend{/reward}, and {idea}none is granted it except the patient.{/idea}
now: Your neighbor complains about your bins again, rudely. The colleague takes credit for your work. {idea}The verse asks for a better reply than the one they gave you.{/idea} Allah knows what they said.
old: If they are rude, I am allowed to be rude back.
new: Answering harm with better is harder and stronger.
try: Answer the next rude message you get with a calm, kind reply.

title: Seek refuge from the devils' prodding.
subtitle: Kindness for people, refuge from Shaytan
then: After teaching kindness to people, Allah teaches a different response to Shaytan: {idea}seek refuge, because no trick helps against them and kindness cannot protect you.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge {trap}from his whisperings, evil suggestions and insinuations{/trap}.
now: That sudden urge to snap at your child. The thought that pops up mid-prayer. The voice saying one more episode, skip Fajr. {idea}You do not have to debate it. Seek refuge.{/idea}
old: I can handle bad thoughts on my own.
new: Whispers are beaten by seeking refuge with Allah, not by arguing.
try: The next time a bad urge hits today, say a'udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim before you act.

title: And refuge lest they come near me at all.
subtitle: Starting every act with Allah's name
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {idea}in any issue of my life{/idea}, so we mention Allah at the start of eating, intimacy and slaughter to ward them off. The Prophet ﷺ sought refuge from {trap}being assaulted by Shaytan at the time of death{/trap}.
now: You grab food from the fridge and start eating without a word. You leave the house in a rush. {idea}A whispered bismillah is a closed door.{/idea}
old: Shaytan only matters in big moments.
new: Mentioning Allah at the start of ordinary acts keeps Shaytan away.
try: Say bismillah before every meal and every time you leave the house today.

title: When death comes, he says: my Lord, send me back.
subtitle: The request everyone will understand too late

row.title: acts of obedience
sub: that is all he will want

then: Ibn Kathir says this is when death comes to {trap}the disbeliever or one negligent with Allah's commands{/trap}. Qatadah said he will not wish to return for family or wealth, {idea}only to obey Allah. May Allah have mercy on a man who does now what the disbeliever will wish he had done.{/idea}
now: You are alive right now, reading this. {idea}You already are the person who got sent back.{/idea} Every day you wake up is the thing he begs for.
old: I will get serious about my faith someday.
new: Today is the second chance others will beg for.
try: Do one act of obedience today that you would wish for if you were on your deathbed.
